_design_note: A06 -> A03: the potential shaping is the only change. This is a research question, not only a hyperparameter. potential_v1's phi is built from BFS distances, so carrying it into the spatial line puts handcrafted domain knowledge back in through the side door. If the anchor learns without it, that is a reportable result about what the CNN discovers on its own; if it does not, the line's dependence on hand-built shaping has to be stated plainly. EXPLORATION SCHEDULE: E09, counted in environment steps rather than rounds. The pilot (runs/m4_pilot_20260827) measured why: at epsilon 1.00 a loot-crate round lasts 9.8 steps because random play kills itself at once, and 210 steps once the agent survives. Under E07's 100-round hold the buffer therefore held 982 of the 10,000 transitions min_size requires, and the first gradient step did not land until round 826 -- with epsilon already annealed to 0.11, which is precisely the cold start E07 existed to provide. E09 holds epsilon at 1.00 for 10,000 steps, exactly min_size, so the first gradient step sees a full buffer at full exploration, then anneals over 200,000 steps.

_predeclared_design_numbers.changed_factor: reward_version A06 -> A03 (identical event table; the shaping term is removed).
_predeclared_design_numbers.control: The M4 anchor arm at the same budget and seeds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.falsification: If A03 matches A06 within 4.7 on loot-crate, the shaping is not carrying this line and should be dropped from the final agent for simplicity.
_predeclared_design_numbers.prediction: None. docs/05 section 0.6 found A06's effect on the handcrafted line was seed-dependent and failed its own safety prediction, so the prior that it matters is weak.
_predeclared_design_numbers.reporting: Quote evaluation_summary.json reportable_result, never selected_checkpoint: the latter maximises over train_seed x checkpoint_round and is biased upward. Report all five training-seed distributions, every G2 threshold, and coins_share alongside score for every arm that has opponents.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_loot_crate: docs/01 section 7.21: the five-seed spread of the handcrafted control gives sd 3.77, so two arms measured once each need a gap of 4.7. That threshold covers training variance; the tournament one below does not.
_predeclared_design_numbers.resolution_tournament: docs/01 section 7.20: pooled 450-round classic-with-opponents score has sd 0.089, so two arms need a gap of 0.246 (coins_share: 0.022). This was measured by re-running ONE fixed set of checkpoints, so it is evaluation noise only and does NOT cover training variance. Use it for a paired same-seed difference, never to bless a maximum taken over seeds.
_predeclared_design_numbers.selection_protocol: Pool the five training seeds at each checkpoint round; pick the round on the pooled VALIDATION curve; freeze it; then read the holdout numbers at that round. Holdout is never used to decide whether to continue an arm.
